about: The levels of the patch pyramid from index `from` on are plates of the place. Inside `deg` (inner, outer, degrees from the spot) they carry their own light: the ground as the close view shows it at the handover, laid back and repainted by assets-src/mercury/place, before the lift and knee of the carry. There the plate holds that picture divided by `gain`. The plates come in by their texels to a pixel, as every level does, so the ground is never softer than its plates. What comes with them is only what the map could not show. `tone` says how: tone.png (written by assets-src/mercury/place/tilt.py, see tilt.json `tone`) is the place's own picture under a Gaussian of `sigmaDeg` degrees, its body; the plate's brightness over that body's (both raised by `floor`, the quotient held under `most`) is its detail, one number a pixel, so it carries no colour of its own. `height` (radii above the ground, from, to) gives a share G that is 0 above the first and 1 under the second, smooth in the logarithm of the eye's height. A plate of the place shows the map's own lit ground at the pixel times that detail at G 0 and its own picture at G 1. Between them the two are mixed by G as powers (each raised by `dark`, the first to the power 1 - G, the second to the power G), so a highlight of the map that the lens has outrun loses its contrast evenly and does not lie on the place's ground as a pale blot; in the dark, well under `dark`, the mix is a straight one, so the map's faint night ground does not go black at once under a plate. At G 1 the globe draws what it drew before `tone`. So the fine craters come by distance, and the craters' bodies and the place's own light come by the eye's height alone. The relief of tilt.json comes with G as well. The first height lies just under the eye's height of the judged dive frame 717, so the hold and 717 hold none of it. `light` and `hold` are options of the globe and both are null in this state. `light` (thin texels of the level before to a pixel: to, from, power) lets the plates' own light come in later than their ground; null, `tone` alone grades it. `hold` (inner, outer, degrees from the spot) keeps the first level in at every distance and the globe's own relief shading out inside that disc; null, the first level comes in by its texels to a pixel. Why null: a first level that holds the place's field from the hold on was built twice and looked at beside the approved image; the judged hold frame 615 lost the hero's ring crater at the spot to a soft dark disc, and the judged dive frame 717 showed a grey disc in the crisp map where the build b0b87889 does not.
